```sql
WITH filtered_orders AS (
    SELECT o.id
      FROM orders o
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
line_items AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           fo.id              AS order_id,
           pv.id              AS variant_id,
           ol.quantity,
           ol.line_total_cents
      FROM filtered_orders fo
      JOIN order_lines ol      ON ol.order_id = fo.id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
),
per_product AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           count(DISTINCT order_id)   AS order_count,
           sum(quantity)              AS quantity,
           sum(line_total_cents)      AS revenue_cents,
           count(DISTINCT variant_id) AS variant_count
      FROM line_items
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       pp.order_count,
       pp.quantity,
       pp.revenue_cents,
       pp.variant_count
  FROM per_product pp
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pp.product_id
 ORDER BY pp.quantity DESC, pp.revenue_cents DESC, p.id
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De orderfilter wordt eerst toegepast zodat de join kleiner begint, en de aggregatie gebeurt op `product_id` alleen (de overige productkolommen zijn functioneel afhankelijk van de primary key). Het extra tiebreaker-kenmerk `p.id` maakt de volgorde bij gelijke `quantity` en `revenue_cents` deterministisch, wat het origineel niet was. De grootste kostenpost, de `count(DISTINCT ...)`-sorteerstap, blijft grotendeels bestaan, dus de winst is naar verwachting bescheiden.
